function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – Mobile Phone Use | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules for merging, turning, and intersections. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• Keep a safe following distance. | TxDOT – Safe Driving Practices | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for all school buses with flashing red lights and extended stop sign.
• Vehicles must stop on both sides of the road. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Pay attention to posted signs for time‑limited or no‑parking zones. | City/County Ordinances | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspections required in some counties (e.g., Dallas, Harris). | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway).
• Use electronic toll tags (e‑Tag, TxTag). | TxDOT – Toll Roads | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights and sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Accident Reporting** | • Report accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 to the police. | TxDMV – Accident Reporting | | **Driving Licenses** | • Must be valid and carry it while driving.
• International drivers may use an International Driving Permit (IDP) for up to 12 months. | TxDMV – Driver Licensing | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text for all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Offers practical guides, safety tips, and updates on road conditions. 3. **TxDMV** – For licensing, registration, and inspection requirements. 4. **Local County Websites** – Often list county‑specific ordinances (e.g., parking, speed limits). --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – especially cell‑phone use; hands‑free is the safest option. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re enforced by both law and technology (speed cameras). - **Respect school bus rules** – stopping for a school bus is mandatory. - **Use proper signals** – give other drivers enough time to react. - **Stay alert for pedestrians** – especially in urban areas and near crosswalks. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent changes, or how to handle a particular driving scenario in Texas!
